reason: Pattern data: the regular expressions Seaready searches other plugins with. Nothing in this file runs a program, writes a file or makes a request.
Finding messages and lists of side-effect names; the only real side effects in Seaready are in check.mjs and git.mjs.
Finding IDs and messages about credentials (SECRET, CREDENTIAL-NAME); no credential is read.
The pattern that looks for permission changes in other plugins; Seaready never changes settings.
Detection pattern for shell: true, not a call.
Detection patterns that name environment variables. Seaready reads only PATH (to find git and claude) and passes its environment to the claude CLI it starts.
Detection patterns that name environment variables.
